problem.text: A data set consists of $6$ (not distinct) positive integers: $1$, $7$, $5$, $2$, $5$, and $X$. The average (arithmetic mean) of the $6$ numbers equals a value in the data set. What is the sum of all possible values of $X$?

steps.title: Where to start: list what the mean could be
steps.body: The mean has to equal a number in the data set, and there are only a few different numbers: $1$, $2$, $5$, $7$ and $X$ itself. So we can try each one in turn. First write the mean in terms of $X$.

your_turn.prompt: What is the sum $1+7+5+2+5$, and what is the mean of all six numbers?
your_turn.answer: The sum is $20$, so the mean is $\frac{20+X}{6}$.

steps.title: Try the fixed values
steps.body: If the mean is a number $m$, then $20+X = 6m$, so $X = 6m-20$. Mean $1$ gives $X=-14$ and mean $2$ gives $X=-8$. Both are rejected, because $X$ must be a positive integer. Mean $5$ gives $X = 10$.

your_turn.prompt: What value of $X$ makes the mean equal to $7$?

steps.title: Don't forget X itself
steps.body: Careful: $X$ is also a value in the data set, so the mean could equal $X$. This case is easy to miss. Set up the equation $$\frac{20+X}{6} = X.$$

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The possible values are $X = 4$, $10$ and $22$. Their sum is $4 + 10 + 22 = 36$. The answer is **(D)** $36$.

wrong_choices.C: This is $10 + 22$, which forgets the case where the mean equals $X$ itself. That case gives $X = 4$, which must be added.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
